species: Multiple (Ankylosauridae, Ceratopsia, Hadrosauridae, Tyrannosauridae, Small Theropoda, Ornithischia, Ornithomimidae, Sauropoda, Stegosauridae)
pose: A stylized, high-fidelity museum exhibit or paleontological field station layout displaying a diverse comparative collection of fossilized dinosaur nests and eggs, cleanly arranged into distinct spatial groups. In the foreground, a detailed, shallow sand-and-mud nest contains a cluster of large, highly elongated, symmetrical cylindrical eggs with rough shell textures (representing large and small theropods and ornithomimids). Adjacent to it sits a mound-shaped dirt nest holding perfectly spherical, rough-textured eggs reminiscent of giant marbles (representing a sauropod clutch). In the midground, a beautifully preserved shallow depression reveals a ring of smaller, slightly teardrop-shaped and oval eggs arranged in a meticulous geometric pattern (representing hadrosaur, ceratopsian, and ankylosaur clades). On the remaining side, a primitive gravel nest displays small, heavily wrinkled or dynamic, oblong egg shapes (representing general ornithischian and stegosaur variants). The background features a softly blurred field tent or laboratory workshop under warm, diffused light, allowing the diverse physical shapes, textures, and arrangements of the fossilized nests to stand out clearly for gameplay identification.
